agent_notes: The diff reverses commit 542d5dd ('General settings fields lived in a separate form from the Save button, so saving never submitted them'). It puts back the form layout that commit fixed, and also deletes the explanatory comments.

Mechanism, read in /Users/julianamacbook/triggarr/triggarr/web/routes.py:529-540: save_settings has no 'preserve current value if field absent' path for General fields. Every field goes through safe_int/safe_log_level with a hard-coded default, and skip_unreleased is a strict == 'on' check. A General field missing from the POST is saved as its default, not left unchanged.

Asymmetry: instances are protected when absent (routes.py:581-594 keeps existing instances if no {app}__ keys are posted), but General is not. Splitting the form is therefore destructive in one direction (instance saves wipe General) and a no-op in the other (General cannot be submitted at all).

Blast radius: every user of the /settings page and every save. The config.toml on disk and the live app.state.settings are both overwritten. Downstream effects: the scheduler's hard_max_per_cycle drops to 0 (unlimited), skip_unreleased turns off, the HTTP client timeout and page size reset, and the log level resets through setup_logging.
No schema or migration changes and no perf impact. It is a template-only change, but its behaviour is a data-loss regression.

Hardening option independent of this diff: make save_settings fall back to current_settings.general.<field> instead of a constant default when a field is absent, so a future form-split mistake cannot wipe config. skip_unreleased would need a hidden sentinel input to tell 'unchecked' apart from 'absent'.
Verdict, blocking issue: General settings get reset on every save. Do not ship. Revert to the 542d5dd form wiring.

findings.fix_hint: Restore id="settings-form" on the instance form and form="settings-form" on all General controls, keeping the Security forms separate.
findings.problem: The General controls now belong to a separate form with no submit button. Clicking Save Settings submits only the instance form, omitting every General field. In triggarr/web/routes.py:531–539, missing values become defaults rather than preserving current settings: for example, hard_max_per_cycle=10 becomes 0 (unlimited), and skip_unreleased=true becomes false. These values are persisted and applied at runtime. General edits therefore cannot be saved through the button, and ordinary instance saves silently disable configured search restrictions.
